To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combined action of phosphate buffer and Ca2+ promotes the fusion of human red cell ghosts.
fusion of human erytrocyte ghosts promoted with the combined action of phosphate and calcium ions.
human erythrocytes fuse in the presence of Ca(2+) and phosphate buffer, and that this fusion is dependent on the Ca(2+)-induced phosphatidyl serine exposure on the membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fusion of human red blood cell ghosts.
the mechanism of membrane fusion, especially the role of Ca2+ in this process.
the mechanism of fusion of human erythocyte ghosts induced by the combined action Ca2+ and PO4– ions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calcium ions are important in the membrane fusion systems.
the fusion of human red blood cell membranes is promoted by Ca2+ and inorganic phosphate ions.
the fusion of erytrocyte membranes is promoted by Ca2+ plus phosphate buffer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ca2+-induced fusion of erythrolysis is inhibited by phosphate buffer, and this inhibition can be reversed by increasing the Ca2+ concentration.
the combined action of phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) and Ca2+ promotes the fusion of erythocyte ghosts, but neither Ca2+ alone nor phosphate buffer alone can do so.

Ca2+, phosphate buffer and the pH of the medium are the most important factors for the fusion of human ghost membranes, and the fusion reaction is dependent on the presence or absence of divalent cation and the pH.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fusion is promoted by Ca2+, but the fusion process itself is not a Ca2+-dependent process.
Ca2+ and PO42– are important for the fusion of biological membranes.
the fusion of human red blood cell ghosts can be triggered by the combined action calcium and phosphate.
